schemaDescription: A raised gold Sol de Mayo emblem on a clear, gold-flecked back — Argentina's most recognized national symbol, worn directly.
card: At the center of this case sits the Sol de Mayo — the sun with a human face that sits between Argentina's two pale-blue flag bands. Molded in raised gold relief over a gold-flecked clear resin back, it traces to the 1810 May Revolution, read ever since as freedom, dawn and new beginnings.
story: At the center of this case sits a raised gold emblem with a face — the Sol de Mayo, or “Sun of May,” the sun that sits at the center of Argentina's flag between its two pale-blue bands. The case reproduces its most recognized feature: a human face at the center of the sun, ringed by alternating straight and wavy rays.

The emblem is molded as a dimensional, metal-effect piece rather than printed flat, set against a crystal-clear back scattered with gold flakes and framed by an electroplated gold edge running the length of the case.

The symbol dates to 1810, when Argentina's May Revolution began the war that ended Spanish colonial rule — the sun is read as freedom, dawn and a new beginning. It's the most directly patriotic piece in the Argentina collection, suited to buyers whose customers want to carry the symbol itself, not just a color palette.

story: A single number carries the weight of this design: the 10. In Argentine football, the No. 10 shirt has meant something beyond a squad number since Mario Kempes wore it to Argentina's first World Cup win — through Diego Maradona's most famous moments, to Lionel Messi finally lifting the trophy in 2022. This case renders that number as a raised, dimensional centerpiece, not a flat print.

The sky-blue and white base is Argentina's own palette, and the gold glitter running along the diagonal split and around the numeral does double duty: it echoes the shine of the World Cup trophy itself, and the three gold stars worn above Argentina's crest — one for each World Cup win.

It's built for a specific kind of buyer: someone whose customers wear this number, not just recognize it — football culture retail, fan merchandise, or Latin American gift shops looking for real specificity instead of generic team colors.

story: This case carries four motifs that run through Aztec and Maya architecture and cosmology, arranged as one continuous field. The stepped pyramid reads as a sacred mountain and a path between earth and sky; the radiating sun stone is drawn from the Aztec calendar stone and stands for the cycles of time; the stepped-fret spiral — one of Mesoamerica's most recognisable marks — signals wind, movement and the union of opposites; the diamond lattice speaks to an ordered cosmos and the four cardinal directions.

None of it is printed. The whole pattern is a same-colour 3D relief pressed into the shell, so it reads as texture in the hand and never fades, chips or peels. The base material is natural wheat straw blended with a biodegradable resin — matte, lightly flexible, and speckled with fine natural wheat-bran flecks that are part of the material, not a finish.

It's built for retailers and gift buyers serving Mexico and the wider Latin American market who want a piece with real cultural depth and an eco story to tell — available across eight colourways and cut for the full iPhone 11 to 18 range.

material: Natural wheat-straw + biodegradable base, matte finish; same-colour 3D embossed motif (laser-engraved / molded)
tagline: A single alebrije — the many-animal spirit-beast of Mexican folk art — pressed in same-colour relief into a matte, biodegradable wheat-straw shell.
metaDescription: Alebrijes Art Biodegradable Case (#DYF2453): Mexican alebrije spirit-beast relief on a matte wheat-straw shell, 8 colourways, fits iPhone 11–18. MOQ 200 pcs / design, lead 15–25 days.
schemaDescription: A single alebrije spirit-beast pressed in same-colour 3D relief into a matte, biodegradable wheat-straw phone case. Eight colourways, fits iPhone 11–18.
card: The alebrije is a Mexican folk-art invention: a fantastical creature built from many animals at once — feline body, wings, horns, a curling serpent tail — covered in dense scrollwork. Born from a craftsman's fever dream in 1930s Mexico City and later carved in Oaxaca, it's read as a spirit guide between worlds, and a celebration of imagination itself.
story: The alebrije is one of Mexico's most distinctive folk-art forms — a fantastical creature assembled from several animals at once: a feline or jaguar body, wings, bull's horns, a curling serpent tail, all covered in dense spirals and feather-like marks. The form traces to Pedro Linares, a Mexico City cartonería maker who saw these beings in a fever dream in the 1930s; woodcarvers in Oaxaca later turned them into the painted copal-wood figures the style is known for today.

In Nahua belief the alebrije is read as a nahual — a spirit guide that moves between the world of the living and the world of the ancestors, associated with Día de Muertos. Many animals in one body stands for strength through fusion; the restless, intricate linework, for a culture that celebrates life loudly.

One large creature fills the back of the case as a same-colour 3D relief — no print, no coating. The shell is natural wheat straw on a biodegradable base: matte, lightly flexible, speckled with natural bran. Eight colourways, cut for the full iPhone 11 to 18 range.

craft.p: The whole alebrije is pressed into the shell in its own colour — a dimensional texture with no ink layer to fade or peel.
Raised camera lip and slim wrap-around edge protect corners and lenses; button covers and ports cut to each model.

story: This design combines two Maya references: blocks of hieroglyphic writing set in cartouches, and Kukulkan — the feathered serpent (Quetzalcoatl in Nahuatl) that appears to descend the stepped pyramid of Chichén Itzá at the equinox.

Maya writing was one of the few complete writing systems of the ancient Americas, used to track astronomy and the Long Count calendar — words cut into stone to last a thousand years. Kukulkan, snake body and quetzal feathers, joins earth and sky; a god of wind, rain, learning and creation, credited with bringing maize and the calendar to people, and read as renewal and cyclical return. Each glyph block is a name, a day, a destiny in the sacred 260-day count.

It's a same-colour 3D relief — no print — on a matte wheat-straw shell over a biodegradable base, speckled with natural bran. Eight colourways, with black reading especially sculptural. Cut for the full iPhone 11 to 18 range.

craft.p: Glyphs and serpent are pressed into the shell in its own colour — a dimensional, stone-carved texture with no ink to fade or peel.

card: Layered fan-shaped arcs reference Art Deco's 1920s fascination with machine-age geometry and symmetry. A deep slate-blue base meets gilded lines for a deliberately luxurious contrast, with fine rhinestones set along every arc for a jewelry-like finish. Drifting gold glitter beneath the resin catches the light like a scattering of stars.
story: Every arc on this case repeats the same fan-shaped curve — layered, mirrored and stacked until it reads as a single continuous pattern. That repetition is deliberate: it's the defining visual language of Art Deco, the early-20th-century style built on machine-age geometry, symmetry and controlled ornament.

The color pairing carries its own weight. A deep slate-blue base sits under sharp gold lines — a combination that reads as composed and a little formal, the kind of contrast associated with classic, high-end design rather than anything trend-driven. Along every curve and edge, fine rhinestones are set into the gold linework, the same "gold-and-gem" logic used in fine jewelry, pushed here into an everyday object.

Underneath the surface, fine glitter and star-shaped sequins sit in the clear resin layer — not part of the printed pattern, but a separate depth that catches light as the case turns in hand. It softens the geometry's precision with something closer to movement, so the case reads differently under different light rather than staying static.
craftHeading: Built to protect, cast to impress.

craft.p: Every fan arc is outlined in gold and lined with fine rhinestones, set by hand along the curve rather than scattered — the density of stones is consistent from piece to piece.

An electroplated metal-effect frame sits flush around the camera module, keeping lenses clear of glare while the raised edge protects against scratches. Button and port cutouts are cut to each phone model's exact layout.
